# House style (public-safe)

The authority for published pages is the SubScout style guide
(https://github.com/AdmcCarthy/SubScout/tree/main/styleguide). This file records only the decisions that
are shared by every output repo (SubScout, Plate, Sheet).

- **Voice:** the interpreter's voice. Confident about the mechanism, explicit about the uncertainty. Impersonal (no "we" or
  "I"), measured, for executive leadership and technically trained colleagues; precise without being academic.
- **Restraint:** Norwegian: function first, just enough, truth to materials, one warm light in a cool room.
- **Type:** Ledger (Newsreader, Instrument Sans, JetBrains Mono). **Palette:** Tide; story palette quiet and
  direct-labelled; categorical palette for identity of 3-5 entities. **Room:** Nordic cool, mørketid at night.
- **Truth gate:** zero baselines, one y-axis, area by area, source/units/confidence on every figure,
  disclosed persuasive choices.
- **Maps:** normalise choropleths, declare classification, state CRS, scale and source resolution.
- **Screens:** desktop first. Design on 1440 × 900, check 1920 × 1080 and 1280 × 720, check a phone at 390 × 844 but do not
  design for it; map frames are landscape, 2.5 : 1 by default and never narrower than 2 : 1 (`house/screens.md`).
- **Print (Plate and Sheet):** real page sizes in mm, type no smaller than 6 pt, vector text, metadata in the
  file, effective resolution stated.
- **Headings and labels:** the article headline may be creative; sub-story, panel and box headings are plain and say what
  is there, and differ in construction from their neighbours, so no device runs the whole piece. The same goes for the shape
  of steps and paragraphs: vary it (SubScout reports repeats as build advice). Appendix label: "Basis of analysis" (not "How we know"). <!-- idiom-ok -->
- **Endings:** a section ends on its last point. No summary paragraph restating what was said.
